Further details on the experimental system and data collection and analysis are also provided in three published papers [Sampath et al [2025, 2024a, 2024b]. The system includes a total of 40 sensors that measure a range of parameters, including those related to the sample (additional sensor details can be found in Sampath et al [2025]). All sensors were connected to two data acquisition units (DAQ), with LabVIEW™ used to acquire and monitor data from these units. The laser spectroscopy sensor operated with a separate program based on Visual Basic and Fortran to gather humidity data. PLC data was collected using RSLinx software, which was used to set up a local OPC (Open Platform Communications) server, while OPC Expert software exported the data from the server into a CSV format for easy readability. The LabVIEW and PLC data were recorded at a frequency of 3.334 Hertz (Hz), equating to one measurement every 300 milliseconds (ms), while the laser data was acquired at a rate of 30 Hz. All collected data was processed using a template created in Excel. Experimental Procedure Experiments were conducted with a focus on the following parameters that closely matched the commercial conditions: • Air temperature: 100°C • Hot-plate temperatures (Chambers 1 and 3): 150°C • Contact pressure: 13.79 kilopascals (kPa), equivalent to 2 pounds per square inch (2 PSI) • Machine speed: 5.08 meters/second (m/s), equivalent to 1,000 feet per minute (FPM) • Air Velocity: ~5 m/s • Contact times setpoints for conduction and convection corresponding to relevant commercial machine speeds, 1000 FPM. Basis weights and paper types included: • 125 GSM (grams per square meter) – Hardwood Unbleached Pulp (Corrugated Medium) • 210 GSM – Softwood Unbleached Pulp (Linerboard) • 300 GSM – Softwood Bleached Pulp (SW Bl; Bleached Board). Laboratory hand sheets were made adhering to the TAPPI standard method T-205. (TAPPI 1992). The sheets were embedded with thermocouples in the middle to measure the sheet temperatures during the drying process. 13 DE-EE0009395 Experimental Calculations: Multiple sensors were employed to accurately capture the drying behavior of the paper samples, ensuring a comprehensive characterization of the process (Figure 2). Based on the weight of the wet sample before the experiment, bone dried sample after the experiment and the instantaneous air flow, temperature, pressure, water vapor concentration at the inlet and outlet of the tunnel, the sheet moisture content, sheet temperature, drying rate were determined as a function of drying time. Based on the measured interior nodal temperatures in the heated platen, the hot surface temperature and instantaneous heat flux were determined using a finite-difference approach to solve the unsteady state one dimensional heat conduction equation [Sampath et al. 2025, 2024b]. Similarly, based on the air flow, temperatures and water vapor concentrations as well as the supplied auxiliary energies, when applied, the net input energy applied to the sample as well as the energy absorbed by the sample as a function of drying time were calculated.
